question:
In the process of bisecting angle BAC in the given figure, why do we draw arcs from points D and E?

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/88b37587aae3130549aad1cd2fc8763ea069609f2f05743075f4c8615d47d4df.png]
solution:
The correct answer is __To intersect above A.__

**__Key Points__**

__
 
• Drawing arcs from points D and E__ is done to ensure that the angle bisector intersects at a point above A.
 
• These intersections help in forming the correct bisector of angle BAC.
 
• The arcs also verify the accuracy of the construction geometrically.
 
• By intersecting above A, it becomes possible to divide the angle into two equal parts.

**__Additional Information__**

 
• **Steps to Bisect an Angle:**

 
 
• Place the compass at the vertex of the angle and draw an arc that intersects both arms of the angle.
 
• From the intersection points on the arms, draw two arcs that intersect above the vertex.
 
• Draw a straight line from the vertex through the intersection point of the arcs above.
 
• This line is the bisector of the angle.
 
 
 
• **Applications of Angle Bisectors:**
 
 
• Used in constructing geometric shapes with precision.
 
• Essential in solving problems involving congruency and symmetry.
